name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
notes: Jointly operated with Andhra Pradesh; masonry dam with 26 flood gates; feeds the Jawahar and Lal Bahadur Shastri gravity canals.

name: Srisailam Dam
notes: Foreshore is the intake for four major lift schemes (KLIS, PRLIS, Dindi, Nettempadu); shared with Andhra Pradesh.

name: Priyadarshini Jurala Project
notes: Uppermost major dam on Telangana's stretch of the Krishna; only Telangana hydro plant with year-round flow; feeds the Bheema and Nettempadu lift schemes.

name: Sriram Sagar Project (Pochampad Dam)
notes: Oldest major Godavari dam in Telangana; its Flood Flow Canal now links into the Kaleshwaram network via Mid Manair Dam.

name: Singur Dam
notes: Principal drinking-water source for Hyderabad (~10 TMC supplied annually); earthen dam.

name: Nizam Sagar Dam
notes: Oldest large dam in Telangana, built under the 7th Nizam; heavily silted (effective capacity now closer to 17.8 TMC).

name: Kaddam Project (Kadem Dam)
notes: FRL reported as 700 ft (~213 m); reallocated as one of the 'existing reservoirs' feeding into the Kaleshwaram scheme's water balance.

name: Lower Manair Dam
notes: Balancing reservoir for the Kakatiya Canal (SRSP); the downstream-most of the three Manair dams.

name: Mid Manair Dam
notes: Central hub of the Kaleshwaram scheme — receives Godavari water lifted from Yellampally and feeds the chain onward to Kondapochamma Sagar.

name: Upper Manair Dam
notes: Oldest of the three Manair dams; foundation laid in 1943 under the Nizam.

name: Sripada Yellampally Project
notes: First major upstream link feeding the Kaleshwaram lift chain onward to Mid Manair; also supplies NTPC Ramagundam.

name: Medigadda Barrage (Lakshmi Barrage)
notes: Godavari intake point of the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme, near the Godavari-Pranahita confluence; a pier subsidence incident occurred in Oct 2023.

name: Annaram Barrage (Saraswathi Barrage)
notes: Second barrage of the Medigadda-Annaram-Sundilla chain; capacity reported as 10.87-11.9 TMC across sources.

name: Sundilla Barrage (Parvathi Barrage)
notes: Third and uppermost Kaleshwaram intake barrage before Yellampally.

name: Kondapochamma Sagar
notes: Terminal reservoir of the main Kaleshwaram trunk; distributes via 13 canals and supplies drinking water to Hyderabad; the '618 m' figure is this reservoir's elevation, not the cumulative lift.

name: Mallannasagar (Komuravelli Mallanna Sagar)
notes: Largest reservoir in the Kaleshwaram scheme, the 'mother reservoir' of KLIS; capacity was enlarged from an original 1.5 TMC design — a politically contested escalation.

name: Ranganayaka Sagar
notes: Intermediate reservoir between Ananthagiri and Mallannasagar.

name: Gouravelli Reservoir
notes: Fed by three 132 MW pumps at Regonda pump house lifting water 126 m; serves the Husnabad area, branching off the Mid Manair chain.

name: Ananthagiri Reservoir (Siddipet)
notes: Intermediate reservoir on Link-4 between Mid Manair Dam and Ranganayaka Sagar; elevation interpolated from neighbouring stages, not independently confirmed.

name: Dindi Reservoir
notes: Main reservoir of the R. Vidyasagar Rao Dindi Lift Scheme, which lifts up to 30 TMC from Srisailam's foreshore across a 12-reservoir network.

name: Osman Sagar (Gandipet)
notes: Built after the 1908 Great Musi Flood to protect and supply Hyderabad; original 5.54 TMC design capacity reduced by siltation.

name: Himayat Sagar
notes: Companion drinking-water reservoir to Osman Sagar for Hyderabad; command area protected from encroachment under GO 111.

name: Kinnerasani Dam
notes: Storage reservoir inside the Kinnerasani Wildlife Sanctuary; coordinates are the sanctuary centroid, not the dam site precisely.

name: Wyra Reservoir
notes: Also receives supplementary water from the Nagarjuna Sagar left canal.

name: Palair Lake
river: Fed by Lal Bahadur (NSP left) canal
notes: Balancing reservoir for the Nagarjuna Sagar left-bank canal; a major freshwater source for Khammam district.

name: Pakhal Lake
notes: Built in 1213 CE by Kakatiya king Ganapati Deva; a 2021 lift scheme from the Godavari augmented storage by ~3 TMC.

name: Ramappa Lake
notes: Built by Kakatiya general Recherla Rudra beside the UNESCO World Heritage Ramappa Temple; nominated as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure.

name: Laknavaram Lake
notes: Kakatiya-era tank with roughly 13 islands linked by a 160 m hanging bridge; irrigates about 3,500 acres.

name: Musi Project Reservoir
notes: Downstream of Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar on the Musi River; irrigates roughly 30,000-42,000 acres.

name: Anjanagiri Reservoir (Narlapur)
notes: First-stage intake reservoir of the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Scheme near Srisailam's foreshore; capacity reported inconsistently (6.4-8.5 TMC) across sources.

name: Udandapur Reservoir
notes: Large balancing reservoir of the Nettempadu / Palamuru-Rangareddy lift network.
